Context/Background: To find novel treatments and drug combinations that could effectively target colorectal cancer cells (CRCs) and lower the probability of disease relapse, we designed multiple different combinations between cisplatin, cannabidiol (CBD), and intermittent serum starvation (ISS) on colorectal cancer cell lines. We analyzed differentially expressed genes and affected pathways in colorectal cancer cell lines to understand further the potential molecular mechanisms behind the treatments and their interactions.
Prompt: Based on the results of the differential expression analysis of CBD vs DMSO in colorectal cancer cells, run a pathway overrepresentation analysis for statistically significant genes (up and down combined) against the Reactome database. Then, provide a discussion of any relevant affected pathways, highlighting important up and down regulated genes in each.  Focus on any mechanisms by which CBD may alter cancer related pathways.
output_text:
Introduction/Context  
A differential expression (DE) analysis was performed on colorectal cancer (CRC) cell lines treated with cannabidiol (CBD) versus DMSO. The input DEG file (ijms-24-14743-v2_crc_cells_cbd_vs_dmso_DEG.csv) contained 20 130 Ensembl genes; applying an adjusted p-value cutoff of <0.05 yielded 2 051 significant DEGs. To identify pathways perturbed by CBD treatment, we conducted an overrepresentation analysis (ORA) of these DEGs against the Reactome_Pathways_2024 library using Enrichr.

Reactome ORA (padj < 0.05; up and down regulated combined) – Top enriched terms  
| Term                                                        | Overlap | Adj. P-value      | Leading Genes (examples)                    |
|-------------------------------------------------------------|---------|-------------------|---------------------------------------------|
| Oncogene Induced Senescence                                 | 16/35   | 1.30 × 10⁻⁵       | RB1; CDK4; CDK6; TP53                        |
| Cytosolic tRNA Aminoacylation                               | 12/24   | 9.11 × 10⁻⁵       | AIMP2; GARS1; AARS1; MARS1                  |
| FOXO-mediated Transcription of Cell Cycle Genes             | 9/17    | 6.10 × 10⁻⁴       | CDKN1B; FOXO3; GADD45A; SMAD3               |
| TP53 Regulates Transcription of Cell Cycle Genes            | 19/49   | 1.33 × 10⁻⁵       | CDKN1B; CCNA2; CCNB1; GADD45A; TP53          |
| Transcriptional Regulation by RUNX3                         | 29/86   | 1.02 × 10⁻⁶       | CCND1; FOXO3; SMAD3; KRAS; TP53              |
| Constitutive Signaling by AKT1 E17K in Cancer               | 11/26   | 8.01 × 10⁻⁴       | AKT1S1; MTOR; RPS6KB2; FOXO3; CREB1          |
| Downregulation of TGF-beta Receptor Signaling               | 11/26   | 8.01 × 10⁻⁴       | SMAD2; SMAD3; TGFBR1; SMAD7                  |
| Toll-Like Receptor 3 (TLR3) Cascade                         | 31/106  | 9.03 × 10⁻⁶       | RELA; MAPK1; JUN; IRF7                      |
| p53-Dependent G1 DNA Damage Response                        | 18/53   | 1.88 × 10⁻⁴       | CDKN1B; ATM; MDM2; TP53; CCNA2               |
| TRIF (TICAM1)-mediated TLR4 Signaling                        | 31/110  | 1.30 × 10⁻⁵       | RELA; MAPK1; IRAK1; TP53                    |

Discussion  
CBD treatment in CRC cells is associated with enrichment of senescence- and cell-cycle control pathways, notably Oncogene Induced Senescence (OR = 7.57) and multiple p53-dependent checkpoints (Adj. P < 1 × 10⁻⁴). Key upregulated inhibitors (CDKN1B/p27, CDKN1A/p21) and effector genes (GADD45A, SFN) suggest CBD may engage a p53/FOXO axis to arrest proliferation. Concomitant enrichment of “FOXO-mediated Transcription” and “Constitutive AKT1 E17K Signaling” reflects modulation of the PI3K/AKT/FOXO balance; for example, CBD-associated downregulation of AKT1 substrates (e.g., RPS6KB2) could relieve FOXO3 activation. Dampening of TGF-β signaling (SMAD2/3, TGFBR1/2) indicates interference with pro-tumorigenic SMAD-mediated transcription. Enrichment of innate-immune cascades (TLR3, TRIF-TLR4) via NF-κB (RELA), MAPK1, IRF7, and JUN suggests CBD may also provoke stress- or pattern-recognition receptor-driven inflammatory responses. Finally, perturbation of tRNA aminoacylation might reflect broad translational control effects. Together, these findings support a model in which CBD induces cell-cycle arrest and senescence through p53/FOXO activation, suppresses pro-proliferative AKT/TGF-β pathways, and modulates innate-immune/stress responses in CRC cells.

Mechanistic highlights  
• Up-regulated cell-cycle inhibitors (CDKN1A/p21, CDKN1B/p27) within p53-dependent and FOXO pathways.  
• Down-regulated AKT-mTOR effectors (RPS6KB2) and TGF-β signaling components (SMAD3, TGFBR1).  
• Activation markers of innate immunity via TLR3/4 cascades (RELA, MAPK1, IRF7).  
• Senescence effectors (RB1, CDK4/6 suppression, TFDP1) in Oncogene Induced Senescence.  

Next Steps & Clarification  
1. Validate p21/p27 induction and p53 status post-CBD treatment by Western blot or qPCR.  
2. Assess AKT/FOXO phosphorylation states to confirm relief of AKT-mediated FOXO inhibition.  
3. Measure TGF-β pathway activity (SMAD2/3 phosphorylation) to verify its attenuation.  
4. Test whether TLR3/4 antagonism alters CBD’s anti-proliferative effect, linking innate-immune signaling to growth arrest.
